scenario.name: CISA AA23-158A, Microsoft & Mandiant — CL0P (TA505 / FIN11) Ransomware: TrueBot Loader, FlawedGrace RAT, SDBbot & Signed Binary Mass Share Encryption (.CIop)
scenario.overview: Imagine a quiet city public library with towering mahogany bookshelves packed with colorful books, green banker lamps on reading tables, a checkout desk, and a locked rare-book cage. Inside the calm public library reading hall, a visitor pulls an index card from the wooden catalog drawer and alters the shelf call-number to point into the staff archive. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the library check-out desk in tiny disguised batches, then smuggles copied records out past the library check-out desk in tiny disguised batches. When the head librarian audits the evening circulation ledger, a restricted rare-book call number checked out on a regular visitor card immediately raises the alarm. In this scenario (T1218.011, CISA AA23-158A, Microsoft & Mandiant, CL0P , TA505 / FIN11 Ransomware: TrueBot Loader, FlawedGrace RAT, SDBbot & Signed Binary Mass Share Encryption .CIop), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: trueBot Execution, then mass Termination of 600+ Processes, then rC4 / AES + RSA-1024 Encryption. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering TrueBot Execution, then Mass Termination of 600+ Processes, then RC4 / AES + RSA-1024 Encryption, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 2: Mass Termination of 600+ Processes & Services (`net stop`) & TinyMet Cobalt Strike Pivot
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion & Impact Preparation (T1489 - Service Stop)
stages.description: Handing that altered slip to the desk clerk under the warm green reading lamps, the visitor gets waved straight past the counter into the restricted rare-book cage. Here in Step 2 inside the public library, the intruder moves quietly past the library check-out desk into neighboring restricted rooms without disturbing the general fiction reading tables. Using TinyMet (a tiny meterpreter/Cobalt Strike stager) to move laterally to domain controllers and file servers, the operator launches the CL0P binary, which contains a hardcoded loop that stops over 600 Windows services (SQLWriter, Veeam, BackupExec, DefWatch) and kills office, database, and backup processes so every file handle on the server is unlocked (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with CodeSigningAbuse=Signed with stolen/expired Authenticode certificate , T1553.002, HardcodedKillList=600+ Windows services and database/backup processes so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
